title: The Ember of the Glass Steppe
premise: Ansel Quintana, a debt-bound scribe in the Glass Steppe's Ledger Guild, discovers that the guild's 'impossible things' are fragments of a stolen moon, sold off piece by piece to buy the border wards' silence. When the wards collapse and the stars go dark, Ansel flees the guildhall with three unlikely allies: Sefa, a disgraced ward-keeper; Bramble, a debt-child raised as collateral; and the Hollow King, a monarch whose crown has been slowly devouring him. As the thirteenth turn of the lightless moon approaches, the usurper wearing the king's shadow moves to complete the trade and seal the Steppe in permanent night. In the end, Ansel burns the master ledger — erasing every debt, including their own — and the found family unbinds the Hollow King at the cost of the guild's power, restoring the stars but leaving the Steppe to govern itself without ledgers, wards, or kings.
about_author: Wren Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing merchant guild records before turning to fantasy. They write stories about people trapped by paperwork and freed by friendship.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ink
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet Ansel copying entries for impossible trades — bottled thunder, a year of someone's luck — while calculating the eleven years left on their own debt. A ledger entry for 'one moon, whole' appears and vanishes within an hour. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine; Ansel longs for belonging but trusts no one.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns of Nothing
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The ward-keeper Sefa reports anomalies along the border: the wards are drinking starlight instead of channeling it. Her superiors dismiss her; her apprentice deserts. That night, the first stars go out above the Steppe. Emotional beat: isolation of the lone truth-teller.

chapters.title: The Guildhall Burns Its Own Books
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ordered to destroy the anomalous pages, Ansel instead copies them into a hidden folio. They are caught by the Guildmaster's enforcer and marked for 'debt reassignment' — a euphemism they've seen end badly. Emotional beat: fear hardening into defiance.

chapters.title: What Falls With the Wards
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. The border wards shatter on the same night the last stars die; refugees pour toward the capital. Ansel escapes the guildhall during the chaos clutching the hidden folio, colliding with Sefa fleeing the ward-towers. Emotional beat: two strangers recognizing each other's desperation.

chapters.title: A Debt Called Bramble
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. A child raised as guild collateral, Bramble knows the vaults better than anyone. They free themselves during the blackout and find Ansel and Sefa hiding in the counting-house cellar, offering passage out in exchange for being treated as a person, not property. Emotional beat: first fragile trust.

chapters.title: The King Who Knocks
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A gaunt man in travel-stained royal colors begs shelter from the trio — the Hollow King, escaped his own palace, where something wearing his crown now rules in his name. He carries a fragment of cold glass that hums like the ledger entries. Emotional beat: pity curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. On the road through the darkened Steppe, the group shelters with a village that has begun governing itself without wards or law. Sefa, trained to enforce order, watches justice happen around a cookfire instead of a courtroom. Emotional beat: her worldview cracking open.

chapters.title: The Thing That Signs His Name
chapters.summary: Hollow King's POV. Flashback interwoven with present: how the crown was offered to him as salvation during famine, how it fed on his memories turn by turn, and how the thing now ruling signs decrees in a hand almost identical to his. Emotional beat: grief for the self he can't fully remember.

chapters.title: Interest Accrued
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The enforcer catches up, offering Ansel full debt-forgiveness to betray the others. Ansel pretends to consider, buying time, and learns the Guildmaster is brokering the final sale: the last moon-fragment to the crown-thing, completing the thirteenth turn. Emotional beat: temptation met with resolve.

chapters.title: Where the Stars Were Kept
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Bramble leads the group through forgotten guild tunnels to the original vault where the moon was first cut apart — now mostly empty, its walls scarred with removal-marks like teeth. Emotional beat: wonder and violation side by side; Bramble claims this place as theirs.

chapters.title: The Cookfire Court
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The village that sheltered them is raided by the crown-thing's bailiffs collecting 'night taxes.' Sefa organizes resistance using ward-craft she was forbidden to teach, and the villagers win a small, costly victory. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, paid for in bruises.

chapters.title: Turn the Eleventh
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. With two turns left, the group deciphers the hidden folio: the fragments answer to the ledger's original ink, which was made from the first extinguished star. One vial survives — in the Guildmaster's private collection. Emotional beat: hope with a terrible price tag.

chapters.title: Homecoming of the Hollow
chapters.summary: Hollow King's POV. The party infiltrates the capital during a coronation-feast celebrating the 'new eternal night.' The Hollow King walks his own halls unrecognized, seeing what his absence built. Emotional beat: a ghost touring his life; he nearly stays lost in it.

chapters.title: The Price of Forgiveness
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel confronts the Guildmaster, who reveals the final cruelty: Ansel's debt was manufactured to bind a scribe capable of reading the moon-ledger. The offer stands — forgiveness for betrayal. Ansel refuses aloud, and alarms wake the palace. Emotional beat: choosing family over freedom.

chapters.title: Escape by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. A chase through the burning archive wing; Bramble steals the star-ink vial while Sefa holds a collapsing stair, and the Hollow King shields them with the last of his borrowed strength. They escape with the vial but lose their maps and half their supplies. Emotional beat: terror braided with fierce loyalty.

chapters.title: Turn the Twelfth
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Camped at the broken border, Sefa rebuilds a single ward-stone as a beacon — not to keep things out, but to call scattered survivors together. Hundreds come. The found family becomes a found community. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: The Crown's Bargain
chapters.summary: Hollow King's POV. The crown-thing offers the Hollow King restoration — his memories, his throne, his name — if he delivers the scribe and the vial. Alone at night, he almost accepts. Instead he writes a letter warning Ansel, in his own hand, proving he is still himself. Emotional beat: the darkest hour before the choice.

chapters.title: Ink Against Night
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The thirteenth turn begins. Ansel prepares to rewrite the master ledger with the star-ink, unbinding every debt — but the ritual requires a debtor willing to erase their own claim first. Ansel burns their own page. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the key that turns the lock.

chapters.title: The Unbinding of the King
chapters.summary: All four POVs interleave. At the palace, the group reaches the crown-thing mid-ritual. Sefa breaks its wards, Bramble shatters the last fragment's casing, and the Hollow King takes back his crown — not to wear, but to break. Emotional beat: climax; fury and love in equal measure.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn, Broken
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The ledger rewritten, the debts dissolved, the crown shattered — the moon completes a turn that ends in dawn instead of darkness. The stars return one by one over the Steppe. The crown-thing unravels into ordinary shadow. Emotional beat: catharsis; light as earned, not given.

chapters.title: What Grows Without Ledgers
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Weeks later: the guild dissolved, villages self-governing, Sefa teaching ward-craft openly, the Hollow King — now just a tired man named Aldric — planting a garden where the vault stood. Bramble, legally nobody's property for the first time, chooses to stay with all of them. Emotional beat: warmth; home as a verb.

chapters.title: The Ember of the Glass Steppe
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, epilogue. Ansel opens a small school for scribes who write only true things, keeping the burned ledger's ash in a glass jar on the desk. A new student asks what the ember inside is. Ansel answers: proof that everything bound can be unbound. Emotional beat: quiet, durable hope; the theme resolved in a single image.
